## Features

- **Dual mode** -- Bot API (httpx) for bots, MTProto (Telethon) for user accounts
- **6 tools** with action dispatch: `message`, `chat`, `media`, `contact`, `config`, `help`
- **Auto-detect mode** -- Set a bot token for bot mode, or a phone number for user mode
- **Local CLI auth** -- `telegram auth` handles the bot token, or phone + OTP + 2FA, on the machine that runs the server
- **Stdio or HTTP** -- stdio by default; HTTP with no-auth (loopback only), a single bearer token, or per-user tokens
- **Tool annotations** -- Each tool declares `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`
- **MCP Resources** -- Documentation available as `telegram://docs/*` resources
- **Security hardened** -- SSRF protection, path traversal prevention, error sanitization, prompt-injection boundary tags on Telegram content

## Install

```
# Claude Code plugin (stdio, bot mode)
/plugin marketplace add n24q02m/claude-plugins
/plugin install telegram@n24q02m-plugins

# Direct uvx invocation (stdio, bot mode)
claude mcp add telegram -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123456:ABC-DEF -- uvx --python 3.13 n24q02m-telegram@latest

# Docker: the image runs the HTTP server and needs a config.toml with
# auth = "token" or "multi" (see HTTP mode)
docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 \
  -v "$PWD/config.toml:/home/appuser/.telegram/config.toml:ro" \
  -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123456:ABC-DEF n24q02m/telegram
```

The package is `n24q02m-telegram` (formerly `better-telegram-mcp`; the old package receives one final release then freezes). The MCP Registry id is `io.github.n24q02m/telegram`, the Docker image is `n24q02m/telegram`, and the legacy `better-telegram-mcp` command is kept as an alias of `telegram`. The pre-rename registry entry `io.github.n24q02m/better-telegram-mcp` stays frozen in the registry and is never republished. Local data moves once from `~/.better-telegram-mcp` to `~/.telegram` on first start.

### Install matrix

| Client | Install |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add n24q02m/claude-plugins` + `/plugin install telegram@n24q02m-plugins` (stdio bot mode), or `claude mcp add` as in the block above |
| Cursor / Windsurf / Gemini CLI / any MCP client | `mcpServers` JSON in the client's config: stdio `command`, or `type: "http"` + `url` pointing at a server you run (see HTTP mode) |

**Install with AI agent** -- paste this to your AI coding agent:

> Install MCP server `telegram` following the steps at [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n24q02m/claude-plugins/main/plugins/telegram/setup-with-agent.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n24q02m/claude-plugins/main/plugins/telegram/setup-with-agent.md)

## Setup

Credentials are configured on the machine that runs the server.

**Bot mode:** set `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` in the client config, or save it once:

```
telegram auth --bot-token 123456:ABC-DEF
```

**User mode:** sign in interactively with your phone number. Telegram sends an OTP; a 2FA password is prompted if the account has one. The Telethon session is stored on disk.

```
telegram auth --phone +15551234567
```

Check the result with `telegram status`. The server reads saved credentials at startup, so restart it after `telegram auth`. Without any credentials the stdio server prints these instructions to stderr and exits with status 1.

## Smithery

Also listed on [Smithery](https://smithery.ai/servers/n24q02m/better-telegram-mcp). Per [`smithery.yaml`](https://github.com/n24q02m/telegram/blob/main/smithery.yaml), Smithery starts the server over **stdio** with `uvx --python 3.13 n24q02m-telegram@latest` and takes **no install-time configuration** (empty `configSchema`). Credentials come from the `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` env var or a prior `telegram auth` (see Setup).

## Configuration

Settings load from `TELEGRAM_`-prefixed environment variables (Pydantic Settings). Env vars take precedence over credentials saved by `telegram auth`.

| Variable | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | Bot mode | Bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) (format `123456789:ABCdef...`) |
| `TELEGRAM_PHONE` | User mode | Phone number in `+<country><number>` form |
| `TELEGRAM_API_ID` / `TELEGRAM_API_HASH` | No | Override the bundled public API pair |
| `USE_BUNDLED_TELEGRAM_CLIENT` | No | Set to `false` to require your own API pair |
| `TELEGRAM_SESSION_NAME` | No | Telethon session file name (default `default`) |
| `TELEGRAM_DATA_DIR` | No | Session directory (default `~/.telegram`) |
| `MCP_TRANSPORT` | No | Set to `http` to start in HTTP mode (`--http` or `TRANSPORT_MODE=http` also work) |

There is no `TELEGRAM_PASSWORD` env var: `telegram auth` prompts for the 2FA password and never stores it in the environment.

## HTTP mode

`telegram --http` serves MCP at `/mcp` and an unauthenticated `GET /health`. Settings live in `~/.telegram/config.toml`:

```
[server]
host = "127.0.0.1"   # default; --host overrides
port = 8000          # default; --port overrides
auth = "token"       # "no-auth" | "token" | "multi"
token_hash = "scrypt$..."
```

| `auth` | Who can connect | Credentials used |
|---|---|---|
| `no-auth` | Anyone who can reach the port; loopback binds only (a non-loopback host is refused) | The default credentials |
| `token` | Clients sending `Authorization: Bearer <token>` matching `token_hash` | The default credentials |
| `multi` | Users listed in `users.toml` (default `~/.telegram/users.toml`), each with their own token | Each user's own namespace |

Create a token hash with `telegram token hash` (it reads the token from stdin or a prompt, never from the command line). In `multi` mode, add users by editing `users.toml` and restarting the server:

```
[users.alice]
token_hash = "scrypt$..."
enabled = true
namespace = "alice"
```

Then authorize Telegram for that user on the server machine:

```
telegram auth --phone +15551234567 --user alice
```

To reach a server on another machine, put it behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy or a private network and use `token` or `multi` auth.

The Docker image (`n24q02m/telegram`, also `ghcr.io/n24q02m/telegram`) runs this HTTP server, not a stdio server: its entrypoint is `python -m telegram --http --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080`, and `MCP_TRANSPORT=stdio` does not change that. Because it binds a non-loopback address, the default `no-auth` mode exits with status 2. Mount a `config.toml` with `auth = "token"` at `/home/appuser/.telegram/config.toml` (for `"multi"`, also mount its `users.toml`). For stdio, use `uvx` or build the `stdio` stage of the Dockerfile (`docker buildx build --target stdio`).

## CLI

The `telegram` console script (installed by `uvx` / `pip`; `better-telegram-mcp` is a legacy alias) starts the MCP server when run without a subcommand. Flags that are not a subcommand are passed through to the server (for example `--http`, `--host`, `--port`).

```
telegram            # start the MCP server (stdio)
telegram --http     # start in HTTP mode
telegram --version  # print the version
```

| Subcommand | Usage | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `auth` | `auth --bot-token <token>` or `auth --phone <+number>`, optional `--user <ns>` | Authorize this machine. Bot mode validates the token; phone mode runs the interactive OTP/2FA flow and stores the Telethon session on disk |
| `login` | Same arguments as `auth` | Deprecated alias of `auth` |
| `logout` | `logout [--yes] [--user <ns>]` | Revoke the Telegram session, delete the session file and the saved credentials |
| `config` | `config status`, `config delete --yes` | Show or delete the saved credential config |
| `status` | `status` | Show whether credentials are configured |
| `doctor` | `doctor` | Print environment diagnostics |
| `token` | `token hash` | Hash a bearer token for `config.toml` / `users.toml` |

`--user` selects the storage namespace (default `default`, used by stdio and the `no-auth` / `token` HTTP modes). Unknown subcommands exit with status 2.

### Tool commands

Every MCP tool is also a one-shot CLI command: `<tool> <action> [flags]` takes the tool's own arguments, calls the same handler the MCP server registers, and connects the backend for that single call -- no server process and no MCP client involved. `--json` prints the tool result as JSON; without it the result is `key: value` lines. A tool error goes to stderr and exits 1.

```
# message: send, edit, delete, forward, pin, react, search, history
telegram message send --chat-id @mychannel --text "deploy is green"
telegram message history --chat-id=-1001234567890 --limit 5 --json
telegram message search --query "invoice" --json

# chat: list, info, create, join, leave, members, admin, settings, topics
telegram chat list --json
telegram chat members --chat-id @mychannel --limit 100

# media: send_photo, send_file, send_voice, send_video, download
telegram media send_photo --chat-id @mychannel --file-path-or-url ./shot.png --caption "nightly"
telegram media download --chat-id 123456789 --message-id 42 --output-dir ./media

# contact: list, search, add, block (user mode only)
telegram contact search --query "An"
telegram contact block --user-id 123456789 --unblock

# settings: status, set, cache_clear -- the MCP tool named `config`
telegram settings status
telegram settings set --key message_limit --value 50

# help: full documentation, no credentials needed
telegram help media
```

The MCP tool `config` is `telegram settings` on the CLI, because `config` is hull's operator command for the saved credential blob. Negative chat ids must be attached with `=` (`--chat-id=-1001234567890`), otherwise argparse reads them as a flag. `--user <ns>` selects the namespace, as for the operator commands.

## Tools

Each tool below is one MCP tool and one CLI group (`telegram <tool> <action>`, see Tool commands); both call the same handler.

| Tool | Actions | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | `send`, `edit`, `delete`, `forward`, `pin`, `react`, `search`, `history` | Send, edit, delete, forward messages. Pin, react, search, browse history |
| `chat` | `list`, `info`, `create`, `join`, `leave`, `members`, `admin`, `settings`, `topics` | List and manage chats, groups, channels. Members, admin, forum topics |
| `media` | `send_photo`, `send_file`, `send_voice`, `send_video`, `download` | Send photos, files, voice notes, videos. Download media from messages |
| `contact` | `list`, `search`, `add`, `block` | List, search, add contacts. Block/unblock users (user mode only) |
| `config` | `status`, `set`, `cache_clear` | Server status, runtime settings (`message_limit`, `timeout`), cache |
| `help` | -- | Full documentation for any topic |

## Comparison

How telegram stacks up against direct competitors in each pillar:

| Capability | telegram | chigwell/telegram-mcp | sparfenyuk/mcp-telegram | guangxiangdebizi/telegram-mcp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bot API mode (bot token) | Yes (httpx) | No | No | Yes |
| MTProto user-account mode | Yes (Telethon) | Yes | Yes | No |
| Send / edit / delete messages | Yes | Yes | No (read-only, draft only) | Yes (send only) |
| Media download from messages | Yes | Yes | Yes | No (send only) |
| Contact management (add / block) | Yes (user mode) | Yes | Partial (list only) | No |
| Multi-user HTTP, per-user isolation | Yes (per-user tokens and namespaces) | No | No | No |
| SSRF protection | Yes (URL validation + DNS-rebinding) | ? | ? | No |
| Path-traversal prevention | Yes | Yes (real-path allowed-root) | ? | No |
| Self-hostable | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## Security

- **SSRF Protection** -- All URLs validated against internal/private IP ranges, DNS rebinding blocked
- **Path Traversal Prevention** -- File paths validated, sensitive directories blocked
- **Session File Security** -- 600 permissions; the 2FA password is prompted, never stored in env vars
- **Error Sanitization** -- Credentials and bot tokens are never leaked in error messages or logs
- **Prompt-injection boundaries** -- Telegram content returned by tools is wrapped in untrusted-content tags

## Build from Source

```
git clone https://github.com/n24q02m/telegram.git
cd telegram
uv sync
uv run telegram
```

## Trust Model

The project does not operate a hosted Telegram endpoint. The server runs on infrastructure you control, and credentials never leave that machine.

| Data | Location | Protection |
|---|---|---|
| Saved credentials (bot token / phone) | `~/.telegram/config.json`; `~/.telegram/subs/<ns>/config.json` in `multi` mode | AES-256-GCM with the machine key `~/.telegram/.secret` |
| Telethon sessions | `~/.telegram/<name>.session`; `~/.telegram/subs/<ns>/` in `multi` mode | File permission 0600 |
| HTTP bearer tokens | `token_hash` in `config.toml` / `users.toml` | Stored only as scrypt hashes |

Anyone with access to your OS user account can read these files.
